s: Moses begins his farewell speeches, recalling the journey from Sinai and the people's refusal to enter the land.
Moses recalls the years of wandering and the first victories east of the Jordan.
The conquest of Og, king of Bashan. Moses asks to enter the land, but God refuses.
Moses urges Israel to keep God's law and never make idols, for no nation has a God so near.
Moses repeats the Ten Commandments given at Sinai.
Hear, O Israel: the Lord is one. Love him with all your heart, soul and strength, and teach his words to your children.
Israel is God's chosen people, not for its greatness but because he loves them. They must not mix with idol worshippers.
Remember how God led you in the desert: man does not live by bread alone.
Israel did not earn the land by its goodness. Moses recalls the golden calf and his prayers for the people.
God gives the tablets again. What he asks is to fear him, love him and serve him.
Blessings follow obedience and curses follow disobedience; the choice is set before Israel.
God is to be worshipped only in the place he chooses.
How to deal with false prophets and anyone who leads others to idols.
Rules on mourning, clean and unclean food, and tithes.
Debts are cancelled every seventh year. Care for the poor and freeing of slaves.
The three great feasts. Judges must be fair.
Rules on judges and courts, and the king, who must study God's law.
The portion of priests and Levites. God will raise up a prophet like Moses.
Cities of refuge, boundary stones and honest witnesses.
Rules for war.
An unsolved murder, captive wives, the rights of the firstborn and a rebellious son.
Various laws on neighbourliness, clothing and marriage.
Who may enter the assembly. Rules on cleanness in the camp, interest and vows.
Divorce, pledges, fair wages and care for the poor, the stranger and the widow.
Fair punishment, the duty to raise up a dead brother's name, honest weights. Remember Amalek.
Firstfruits are offered with thanksgiving. Israel is God's own people.
The law is to be written on stones on Mount Ebal, and curses are pronounced for wrongdoing.
The blessings of obedience and the many curses that will follow disobedience.
The covenant is renewed in Moab. The hidden things belong to God, the revealed to us.
If Israel returns to God, he will gather them again. Choose life.
Moses hands leadership to Joshua and gives the law to the priests to be read every seven years.
Moses' song tells of God's faithfulness and Israel's unfaithfulness. He is told he will see the land from afar.
Moses blesses each tribe of Israel.
Moses views the promised land from Mount Nebo and dies. No prophet has arisen in Israel like him.

6: This is the heart of Israel's faith: one God, loved with all your heart, soul and strength. Jesus calls it the first and greatest commandment.
18: God promises to raise up a prophet like Moses. The early Christians recognized this prophet in Jesus.
34: Moses sees the promised land but does not enter it. The leadership passes to Joshua, whose name is the same as Jesus.
